title: Ops weekend preflight: executive reads + all-team run-of-show
content:
Purpose:
This is the preflight checklist and executive-reads packet for the upcoming ops weekend + company sync. Primary goals: 1) finalize company-level OKR wording for Q3 draft, 2) lock the all-team run-of-show and slide owners, 3) rehearse escalation lanes and fallback messaging.

Audience:
Exec team, program leads, comms, product-ops, people ops.

High-level summary (what changed since last draft):
- Condensed OKR objective language to be customer-facing-friendly (see OKR section).
- Added explicit fallback model in case CI noise triggers last-minute topic pull (Section: Escalation & Fallback).
- Rehearsal schedule tightened: two dry runs instead of three (primary + quick-fire).
- Reworked exec-read one-pager for legal/compliance ask clarity.

Run-of-show (live 90 min) - anchored times are relative to 09:00 PT start:
- 09:00 - 09:05: Opening (CEO) - framing: "What winning looks like in H2" (Maya Patel)
- 09:05 - 09:20: Product slate (3 quick demos) + ask for partner teams (Laura Chen)
- 09:20 - 09:35: Ops reliability snapshot: SLOs, incidents, mitigations (Diego Marquez)
- 09:35 - 09:50: Roadmap and commitments (top company OKRs + bold bets) (Ethan Wu)
- 09:50 - 10:10: People and org changes + hiring asks (Priya Raman)
- 10:10 - 10:25: Customer stories + wins (Customer Success lead - TBD)
- 10:25 - 10:40: Live Q&A - prepopulated Q bank first, then live (Moderator: Maya)
- 10:40 - 10:45: Wrap + next steps (CEO)

Slide ownership (quick map):
- Opening slide + framing: Maya Patel
- OKR slides: Ethan Wu + product ops (2 slides)
- Reliability + SLOs: Diego Marquez (3 slides; include 30/60/90 mitigation lane)
- People slide: Priya Raman (hiring roadmap + org changes)
- Customer wins: CS lead (one slide; script included below)

OKR DRAFT (company-level, language intentionally customer-facing; KR targets rough placeholders):
Objective A: Make inference predictable at scale (economic and latency predictability)
- KR A1: Reduce 95th p99 latency variance across top-10 routes by 25% vs baseline (owner: serving-runtime)
- KR A2: Improve price-per-1M-token efficiency by 18% on production workload via batching + quantization playbook (owner: optimize)
- KR A3: Ship model routing autopilot with cost/latency policy support and 2 customer pilots (owner: platform-engineering)

Objective B: Deliver enterprise-ready private deployments with frictionless onboarding
- KR B1: Complete VPC onboarding flow automation + docs for 3 pilot customers (owner: private-deployments)
- KR B2: Install KMS/HSM integration in staging for all private plans (owner: security-and-compliance)
- KR B3: Achieve 99.9% availability SLA on Dedicated during reserved-hour windows for pilot customers (owner: dedicated)

Objective C: Improve developer-to-production time for LLM features
- KR C1: Reduce mean time from prototype to productionized route by 35% (owner: developer-experience)
- KR C2: Ship SDK improvements and two sample apps demonstrating latency/cost tradeoffs (owner: developer-experience + examples)
- KR C3: Increase in-product adoption of Optimize suggestions by 20% for teams with >$2k monthly usage (owner: optimize)

Notes on OKRs: these are intentionally lean; we should limit public slides to Objectives + 1 KR each to avoid scaring customers. Detailed KR table reserved for exec-read appendix. Confirm KR numeric targets by Friday EOD.

Escalation & Fallback map (Preflight lanes):
- Lane 1 (Product optics failure): If demo breaks during live demo -> immediate switch to recorded demo (Laura has recording link). Announce brief pause (30s) and proceed.
- Lane 2 (CI/incident chatter spikes): If SRE detects active SEV with customer impact during all-hands -> move incident note into appendix and switch to high-level mitigations only. Notify #allhands-ops with short blurb: "We will follow up with a dedicated incident update after the sync."
- Lane 3 (Exec time bleed): If timing slips >7 minutes by 09:35 -> collapse People + Customer into single 10-min block; push deep-dive content to follow-up digest.

Script excerpts (short bullets for speakers):
- CEO opening: one-liner mission reframe, three concrete signals of momentum, one call to action for teams. Avoid product-level minutiae.
- Product: 30s context per demo, what changed, why it matters to latency/cost. End with explicit ask: "we need two cross-functional engineers for pilot X".
- Reliability: show trend chart, two root causes addressed, one ask of product: "please decompose route X to allow caching".

Q bank (prepopulated - use these first in Q&A):
- Q: "How will Dedicated SLAs affect hosted pricing?" A: Short answer + link to pricing review doc (Ethan)
- Q: "Are we pausing model additions while optimizing runtime?" A: No. We will prioritize onboarding that has performance profile documentation (Research lead).
- Q: "What does private deployment timeline look like for regulated enterprise?" A: We share pilot milestones and expected go-live window (Priya).

Action item tracker (owner / due):
- Finalize OKR numbers for public slide (Ethan Wu) / due 2025-06-13
- Lock slide deck + speaker notes, upload to /releases/allhands/ (Maya Patel) / due 2025-06-12 15:00 PT
- Create recorded demo link and add to appendix (Laura Chen) / due 2025-06-12 12:00 PT
- Prepare incident-message template for SRE (Diego Marquez) / due 2025-06-12 18:00 PT
- Draft follow-up digest email and cadence for Q&A answers (Comms) / Priya Raman / due 2025-06-13

Rehearsal plan (today + day before):
- Dry run 1 (full run): 2025-06-12 09:00 PT - mandatory for slide owners + execs (recorded). Focus: transitions and time-boxing.
- Dry run 2 (quick-fire): 2025-06-13 08:30 PT - mandatory for moderator + host + product leads (15-20m). Focus: Q&A flow and fallback drills.
- Capture feedback in this doc under section "rehearsal notes" and in the quick Google Form (link in linked_artifacts).

Communication & distribution plan:
- Immediate: exec-read one-pager (attached) to execs + leads 48 hours before event.
- T-minus 24h: full deck to all employees with placeholder follow-up time slots.
- T-minus 6h: Slack reminder + checklist ping to slide owners.

Open questions / decisions needed (priority order):
1) Confirm KR numeric targets and owners for KRs flagged as "owner: optimize" (who is primary owner?) - action: Ethan to confirm by 2025-06-13.
2) Who is the customer success lead presenting the story? (Priya to confirm)
3) Decide whether to include a short live demo of private deployment (risk: networking flakiness) - proposal: recorded demo if any doubt.

Last-minute preflight checklist (10 items):
- [ ] Video recordings uploaded + tested (Laura)
- [ ] Backup slide deck (PDF) uploaded to shared drive (Maya)
- [ ] Moderator script printed + Slack channel staged (Maya)
- [ ] Incident message template ready (Diego)
- [ ] Exec read one-pager approved by legal (Priya)
- [ ] Zoom/webcast tech check with comms (Comms)
- [ ] Accessibility captions enabled for webcast (People Ops)
- [ ] Follow-up digest template ready (Comms)
- [ ] Q bank finalized and owner responses drafted (Moderator)
- [ ] Recording + transcription enabled for post-event notes (Maya)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep OKR language short. Execs prefer crisp, non-technical KR phrasing for town.
- If we need to cut content, drop org-level depth, keep product + reliability.
- Collect 2-3 micro-stories from CS customers that highlight latency/cost wins — short bullets only.

Rehearsal notes (to be filled during dry runs):
- 2025-06-12 Dry Run 1: [placeholder for timing slips, awkward transitions, audio issues]
- 2025-06-13 Dry Run 2: [placeholder for Q bank refinement]

Appendix: exec-read one-pager checklist (attach in deck appendix) - include top-line numbers, 2-3 mitigation bullets per open risk, and direct asks (resourcing/hiring/approval).

If anything needs to be reworded for external customers, highlight it now and route to PR/comms for approval.

-- end of doc --
